chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah al-Halabi from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan differed regarding a man who dies and has no 'asabah (agnates) to inherit him, but has a close relative who does not inherit.
Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'His inheritance is for them,' citing the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And those of the womb (close relatives) are closer to one another [in inheritance].'
And 'Uthman said: 'It is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.أُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ: Those of the womb (close relatives, typically maternal or non-agnatic)
key_terms.بَيْتُ مَالِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The treasury of the Muslims (state treasury)
key_terms.ذُو قَرَابَةٍ: Close relative (often referring to those with a specific share or residual right, distinct from 'asabah)
key_terms.عَصَبَةٌ: Agnatic heirs (male relatives who inherit by virtue of their male line)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali and 'Uthman differ on the inheritance of relatives without agnatic heirs?
ai.summary: This narration highlights a foundational jurisprudential divergence between Imam Ali and Caliph Uthman regarding the distribution of estate to non-agnatic relatives when no 'asabah (male lineal heirs) exist. While Uthman directed the wealth to the general treasury (bayt al-mal), Imam Ali invoked the principle of 'qurb al-rahim' (closeness of kinship) to prioritize blood relatives, a view that underscores the Shia emphasis on the Quranic text's explicit inclusion of maternal and paternal kin in inheritance shares.
